The results of the qualifications and research proposal evaluation, as well as the oral examination detailed schedule,

the bottom of the page). No personal written communication will be sent to applicants concerning the examinations

During the oral examination, applicants may express their interest in one or more PhD positions linked to specific
research topics.
Required and Supporting Documents to be attached to the application
Only documents in Italian or English will be considered valid and will be assessed by the Admission Board. Identity
documents and diplomas/degree certificates issued in a language other than Italian or English must be accompanied by
an official translation. The translation must be carried out by an authorized body or by the awarding university.
Only qualifications obtained in the last 5 years will be taken into account, with the exception of university degrees. The
Admission Board will assess the relevance of the supporting documents to the PhD programme.

REQUIRED DOCUMENTS
Identity document Valid identity document with photo (i.e. identity card, passport)
Degrees Documents attesting the awarding of the first and second cycle degrees, the exams taken and
the marks obtained (see Art. 3 of the Call for Applications)
Curriculum Vitae The Curriculum Vitae must be drawn up exclusively using the Curriculum Vitae form, which is
downloadable as a .docx file from the University website (select the PhD Programme → “More
information”, then check “Notices” at the bottom of the page). Applicants not using the
attached form shall be excluded from the qualifications evaluation.
The section “Preferred Principal Investigators (mandatory)” must be completed, indicating
your preference for three supervisors for the 42nd cycle PhD programme. Further details
regarding each supervisor’s research areas can be found on the Faculty Members page.
Research proposal The research proposal must be drawn up exclusively using the Research Proposal form,
which is downloadable as a .docx file from the University website (select the PhD Programme
→ “More information”, then check “Notices” at the bottom of the page). Research proposals
that do not comply with this requirement shall not be evaluated.
The three-year research project must be proposed by the candidate within the scope of the
PhD programme’s research areas, as detailed on the Faculty Members page. Please note that
the project submitted will not constitute the research topic that the candidate, if admitted,
will undertake during the PhD programme. This project will be agreed with the Supervisor and
must be approved by the Academic Board, in accordance with the main research topics of the
programme and the research topics linked to the available PhD positions (see “Available
Positions and Scholarships” table, column “Positions linked to research topics”).
The assessment of the project is aimed at ascertaining the candidate’s ability to organise
research work effectively, their understanding and appropriate application of experimental
methodologies, as well as the project’s consistency with the main research topics of the PhD
programme in Molecular and Cell Biology, rather than the absolute originality of the scientific
idea.
In accordance with the University's policy on the ethical and responsible use of Generative
Artificial Intelligence in teaching and research activities, candidates must explicitly state
whether they have used Generative Artificial Intelligence systems in the production of the
research proposal attached to their application form, specifying which tools were used and for
which parts of the document. During the oral examination, the Admission Board will assess the
candidate's full mastery of the content included in the document and their ability to justify the
methodological and scientific choices made in the project.
